# Research programme

::: {.ac-section .ac-research-section}
## Monetary regimes and central banking {#monetary-regimes-and-central-banking}

I study Czechoslovak monetary policy during the Great Depression: the defence of the koruna, reserve requirements, central-bank balance sheets, and the devaluations of the 1930s. The work examines how monetary choices affected credit, prices, output and employment.

Current projects reconstruct effective exchange rates and investigate the relationship between monetary defence, central-bank law and domestic contraction. They draw on the reports of the National Bank of Czechoslovakia, contemporary policy debates and monthly economic series.

[Related papers](publications.qmd#research-manuscripts)
:::

::: {.ac-section .ac-research-section}
## Financial stress and banking {#financial-stress-and-banking}

My financial-stress project combines eleven monthly indicators for Czechoslovakia from November 1929 to September 1938. It reconstructs the timing of monetary and banking pressure and compares it with the downturn in the real economy.

The project uses central-bank balance sheets and market indicators to examine financial pressure that is not captured by a chronology of bank failures alone.

[Measuring Financial Stress under the Gold Standard: dataset and documentation](data.qmd#financial-stress-under-the-gold-standard)
:::

::: {.ac-section .ac-research-section}
## Exchange rates and trade adjustment {#trade-devaluation-and-commercial-reorganisation}

I examine how devaluation, exchange controls and changes in relative prices affected European trade during the interwar period. This work combines monthly exports, imports, prices, economic activity and exchange rates with annual bilateral trade weights.

The Missing J dataset covers 1925–1936 and supports comparisons of nominal and real effective exchange rates and the timing of trade-balance responses.

[The Missing J dataset](data.qmd#the-missing-j)
:::

::: {.ac-section .ac-research-section}
## Historical national accounts {#historical-measurement-and-output-reconstruction}

With Matthias Morys and Marcin Wroński, I am developing the Czechoslovak contribution to a comparative reconstruction of interwar Central and Eastern European GDP.

The current work focuses on agricultural output and value added. It brings together production quantities, prices and intermediate inputs and examines how differences in sources and sectoral coverage affect comparisons across countries.
:::

::: {.ac-section .ac-research-section}
## History of economic thought {#economic-thought-as-a-policy-institution}

My doctoral research examined Czech economic apriorism, especially the work of Karel Engliš, Jan Loevenstein and František Weyr. I continue to study their approaches to economic method, theories of crisis and monetary policy.

Current work includes Loevenstein’s theory of underconsumption and technological unemployment, Engliš’s monetary policy, and debates over taxation and social policy in interwar Czechoslovakia.

[Working papers and current projects](publications.qmd#projects-in-development)
:::
:::
